summary:
(AstraVital) - Astronaut Health Intelligence & Monitoring System

AstraVital is an offline-aware astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew members in assessing and managing their health during space missions. It provides personalized health workspaces where astronauts can record six essential health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and mood. The system compares measurements against individual health references, identifies explainable changes and trends, and provides an interactive dashboard for reviewing health history. It also features an interactive body explorer, health guidance, scheduled assessments, and an emergency response center for recording incidents and following step-by-step demonstration workflows. By bringing essential health information and monitoring capabilities into one accessible platform, AstraVital addresses the challenges of astronaut self-assessment during long-duration missions, particularly when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. Its offline-aware architecture supports onboard access, while its simulated emergency and communication workflows demonstrate future possibilities for autonomous spaceflight medical support.
details:
Project Details | AstraVital

What does AstraVital do and how does it work?

Astronauts living and working in space experience conditions that can affect their physical and psychological health. Changes in gravity, radiation exposure, isolation and the spacecraft environment can create health challenges that become particularly difficult to manage during long-duration missions. We developed AstraVital, an astronaut health intelligence and monitoring platform, to help crew members monitor their health, understand changes in their condition and maintain personal health records throughout a mission.

AstraVital provides astronauts with an individual health workspace where they can record six important health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration and mood. Each observation can include its measurement time, unit, source and additional notes. The system compares recorded measurements against the astronaut's own personal health references rather than relying entirely on generic population values.

One of the main features is its explainable health-monitoring system. Instead of simply displaying measurements, AstraVital identifies differences from established personal references and presents understandable signals explaining why a measurement may require further review. It also distinguishes between missing information, insufficient historical data, measurements requiring verification and trends that need attention. This helps prevent incomplete information from being mistakenly interpreted as a healthy result.

The platform also includes an interactive human-body explorer that allows astronauts to select different body regions and explore possible relationships between spaceflight conditions and human health. Its Health Guide provides information about the major hazards of spaceflight and their potential effects on the body.

Another important component is the Emergency Response Center. Crew members can record medical incidents, access demonstration-only step-by-step workflows and track their progress. The application also includes monitoring schedules and a simulated communication outbox to demonstrate how medical information could be prepared for transmission to ground-based medical personnel.

What benefits does it provide?

AstraVital brings several important health-monitoring functions together in one accessible platform. It helps astronauts maintain organized personal health records, compare current observations with individual references, identify potentially concerning changes and understand why certain measurements deserve attention.

Its explainable approach makes health information easier to understand, particularly for crew members who are not medical specialists. The application also considers the communication challenges of deep-space missions by providing an offline-aware architecture and locally accessible application resources.

Rather than treating health monitoring as simply collecting numbers, AstraVital focuses on connecting measurements with meaningful information and appropriate next steps.

Intended impact

Our intended impact is to support greater medical awareness and health-monitoring autonomy during long-duration human space missions. As astronauts travel farther from Earth, delayed communication can make timely medical support more challenging. Providing an organized way to record observations, review health trends and access relevant medical information could help crews and their medical support teams make better-informed assessments.

AstraVital is designed as a prototype demonstrating how digital health monitoring and onboard decision-support capabilities could contribute to safer and more independent human space exploration.

Technology and tools used

We developed AstraVital as a web application using React, TypeScript and Vite for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering the backend. We used Pydantic for data validation, SQLite for database persistence, and Recharts for health-data visualization. We also used Dexie.js for browser-side data management, alongside a Progressive Web App structure and service worker for offline-aware application access.

Python dependencies are managed using Astral UV. Git and GitHub are used for version control and project management. The application is deployed using Vercel for the frontend and FastAPI Cloud for the backend.

Currently, health measurements are primarily entered manually. Real medical-device, spacecraft telemetry and ground communication integrations have not yet been implemented.

What makes AstraVital creative?

What makes AstraVital different is its focus on individual health references and understandable health insights rather than displaying isolated medical measurements. It combines personal health monitoring, historical trends, interactive anatomical exploration, spaceflight-health education and emergency incident management in one application.

We also considered the practical conditions of human spaceflight, including delayed communication, limited connectivity, the need for clear interfaces and the importance of distinguishing actual health observations from missing or insufficient data.

We designed AstraVital around a simple idea: astronauts should not only be able to record their health, but also understand what their information means and why it may matter during a space mission.
